title: Polynomial-time language indicators
statement: Let $V$ be a language over the binary alphabet and suppose $V$ belongs to $mathsf{P}$. Then the function sending each binary string $x$ to the one-bit string containing $1$ if $x\in V$ and $0$ otherwise is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: $V$ is a language over the binary alphabet
replaced:
Let $V \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ be a language in $\mathsf{P}$, and let
$\mathbf{1}_V(x)$ be the bit $1$ if $x \in V$ and $0$ otherwise. Then the map
sending a binary string $x$ to the one-bit string $\mathbf{1}_V(x)$ is
polynomial-time computable: some finite multi-tape Turing machine over the binary
alphabet computes it within $D(n+1)^d$ steps on every input of length $n$, for
some constants $D, d \in \mathbb{N}$.
